Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Thanks — quick clarifications on SSO / KMS / logging for deployment sizing

Alicia / Gabe,

Thanks again for carving out time today. Helpful call — I wanted to capture the small set of infra constraints that will drive whether we recommend Hosted, Dedicated, or Private for your production rollout. Quick recap + two asks: what you confirm, what we advise.

High-level notes from the call:
- Primary requirement: patient PII will be in inference payloads for certain endpoints (deidentified sets for others).
- Identity: enterprise Okta + SAML required across all end-users; IdP provisioning will be handled by your IAM team.
- Keys: you need hardware-backed key storage for certain data paths (you mentioned an HSM requirement for signing).
- Logging: audit logs to be retained off-platform for 7 years; ability to ship syslog/SIEM events in near real-time.

Two asks for you (short answers are fine):
1) Confirm whether BYOK with your HSM (on-prem HSM or cloud HSM in customer-controlled project) is mandatory, or if BYOK-KMS (cloud-managed KMS under your control) is acceptable as an interim?
2) Which latency SLO matters most for the initial rollout: P99 < 300ms (interactive) or are 500–700ms acceptable if we use batching for cost optimizations?

What we recommend given the constraints – subject to your answers above:
- If HSM is mandatory and we must not hold keys, Private (VPC or on-prem) is likely required.
- If BYOK via cloud KMS is acceptable and you can tolerate dedicated networking, Dedicated capacity in a customer project gives predictable throughput and lets us integrate KMS without full Private control.
- Hosted API only if you can relax HSM/BYOK or accept a managed KMS model and stricter tokenization of PII.

Next steps:
- Alicia, Gabe: please reply with the two answers above and any redlines for retention or regulatory audit windows.
- Ill loop product/security for an implementation plan once we have your answer.

Attaching a short one-pager that compares Dedicated vs Private focusing on identity, keys, and logs.

Cheers,
Diego
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Diego,

Thanks for the concise summary. Answers below: 
1) HSM-backed keys are required for signing of patient-related artifacts. Were open to cloud HSM (e.g., Google Cloud HSM or AWS CloudHSM) but keys must remain in our tenant/account and we need a BYOK flow. We cannot use a fully-managed Redwood KMS that holds key material.
2) For the initial pilot we can accept P99 ~ 500ms, but for go-live our product team will want a P99 target closer to 300ms. That will influence planned concurrency.

Also: the security team wants to ensure audit events (access, key-usage, config changes) are exported to our SIEM and retained for 7 years. We can start with 1-month hot retention and then archive to cold storage.

Let us know what you need from our infra folks to validate the BYOK flow.

Best,

Diego / team / Alicia,

Quick technical readout from my side after a 1:1 with infra: 
- Dedicated: We can run Dedicated capacity in a customer project and integrate customer CloudHSM / CloudKMS using a BYOK flow for key wrapping and signing. Caveats: (a) most cloud HSMs used in BYOK mode still require a network path from our serving hosts into the customer's project; wed need peering or private networking; (b) latency is typically fine for your pilot target (P99 ~500ms) but achieving 300ms P99 at scale with HSM calls on the critical path will require local key-caching patterns and likely an HSM proxy in the same VPC as the serving cluster.
- Private (VPC-hosted or on-prem): gives the cleanest separation (no cross-tenant key hops) and simplest compliance story for long-term audits. Also easier to guarantee log forwarding to a customer-controlled SIEM with 7y retention. Operationally, Private adds onboarding overhead (networking, subnets, CA certs) and has a longer lead time (2-6 weeks depending on customer's infra).

My recommendation: start the Pilot on Dedicated with a cloud-HSM BYOK integration and a pre-agreed HSM proxy pattern in the same VPC to hit the 500ms pilot SLO. Run a parallel plan to validate Private deployment for go-live if the security team keeps HSM-as-mandatory and long retention. That gives Calyx faster time-to-value while we lock down the long-term compliance model.

Ill prepare a short diagram and list of infra artifacts we need from Calyx (VPC details, HSM project id, SIEM endpoint, SAML metadata).

-Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Adding a compliance view: 
- Audit & retention: 7-year retention of audit logs with customer control is non-negotiable for their compliance team. We can stream logs off-platform (syslog/HTTPS) from either Dedicated or Private, but Dedicated will require careful SLA around guaranteed delivery and replay for long-term archiving; Private makes archive ownership explicit.
- Key custody: if Calyx requires hardware key custody (HSM where they control the tenant and key material), Private is the lowest friction path. Dedicated + BYOK cloud-HSM works but we need a runbook for cryptographic separation and evidence (key rotation logs, HSM access logs) that meets auditors.
- Recommendation: Proceed with Marissas suggested pilot on Dedicated with explicit agreements: (a) BYOK via customer CloudHSM, (b) HSM proxy pattern in-customer VPC, (c) nightly archive push to customers cold storage and weekly integrity checks. Parallel validate Private for go-live and include a SOC2 attestation package in the POC.

Ill draft the security checklist items we need from Calyx for the runbook.

- Rishi
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
